correctness.rationale: The Dirichlet covariance identity yields the explicit affine reproducing kernel. Its first-variable affinity and full-support sign disagreement prove strict vertex reduction. Beta truncated moments yield the exact norm/negative-part formula. A three-cell Dirichlet aggregation coupling and strict conditional Jensen show that normalized Beta coordinates are strictly decreasing in convex order with increasing shape at fixed total, selecting precisely the least-parameter vertices. Fractional beta moments justify the rare-coordinate supremum; a beta CLT plus bounded second moments justifies the Gaussian regime. The actual standalone verify.py reproduces the moment identity and 275 rational beta-integral checks. The general theorem is analytic, not based on finite enumeration.

The Griffiths–Spanò full text supplies the general degree-one kernel, not a norm-optimization, negative-part/least-coordinate theorem or fixed-total balancing principle. Published polynomial-mesh numerical results give general evaluation algorithms, not the exact weighted norm and ordering. No stronger encompassing claim was found in the actual scientific searches. Equivalent literature remains a residual risk, notably a Jacobi-kernel paper inspected only at abstract level.

value.rationale: The exact norm of a natural least-squares projector under arbitrary Dirichlet sampling controls worst-case amplification and positivity loss. The least-coordinate principle is a complete structural classification of instability: only the smallest concentration and total matter, and precisely the rarest-coordinate vertices are extremal. The unique balancing minimum, sharp unattained 2A+1 boundary, and Gaussian high-concentration growth give directly motivated design/stability consequences. These go beyond a uniform-weight recomputation and are not an arbitrary finite slice.
